verdicts.quote: The proposed default is one reminder occurrence per invoice for the lifetime of that invoice. ... The first eligible date is the next local calendar date.
Suppress drafts and other unissued invoices, paid or zero/credit-balance invoices, voided or canceled invoices, and invoices marked non-collectible or subject to an authoritative collections hold.
verdicts.missing: Whether disputed invoices and payment-plan invoices stop reminders is deferred to the billing owner ('holds (including any disputes or payment-plan states)' is an open gap).

verdicts.quote: gives the due date and current outstanding amount with currency ... A partial payment before authorization changes the balance used for the message if the invoice remains eligible.
A missing, invalid, ambiguous, revoked, or suppressed recipient ... yields no handoff. ... The billing owner must confirm the approved contact-selection and suppression rules
verdicts.missing: Which customer states (do-not-contact, paused, unsubscribed) count as suppression, and whether a billing notice is exempt from a marketing opt-out.

verdicts.quote: Each account and immutable invoice pair has one logical occurrence. Overlapping evaluations, repeated triggers, and restarts converge on the same occurrence. Confirmed channel acceptance prevents a further dispatch for that occurrence.

Before dispatch authorization, use current policy, automation authority, invoice status, balance, due date and recipient. ... A stale discovery read can identify a candidate but cannot grant dispatch authority.
Definitive temporary non-acceptance can be retried within an approved retry policy ... Permanent rejection or retry exhaustion ends automated attempts with an actionable status.
verdicts.missing: Retry delays, deadline and attempt cap are left open, and nothing says how a person is alerted beyond a readable status.

verdicts.quote: Backpressure or rate limiting preserves recoverable status and applies R-4 when a retry is due. ... Open bounds are ... backlog and burst workload, delivery rate and resource quotas
verdicts.missing: The provider's rate limit and how a large batch is paced within it are not specified.

verdicts.quote: This includes ... eligible invoices already overdue at activation. ... The maximum allowed age for catch-up and handling of very old invoices are open product decisions.
verdicts.missing: How the backlog is paced or limited so it does not all go out at once at activation.

verdicts.quote: the billing account's local calendar date is later than that due date. The first eligible date is the next local calendar date.
verdicts.missing: Sending hours, business hours, weekends and holidays are not addressed; only the date boundary uses local time.

verdicts.quote: gives the due date and current outstanding amount with currency
verdicts.missing: How amounts and currency are formatted for the recipient (locale, symbol, decimals).

verdicts.quote: A missing, invalid, ambiguous, revoked, or suppressed recipient ... yields no handoff. The authorized operator can distinguish the actionable reason. ... If the selected channel supplies an authoritative bounce report, expose it as a delivery failure
Send to the current authorized billing contact selected for the invoice. ... A missing, invalid, ambiguous ... recipient ... yields no handoff.
verdicts.missing: The rule for choosing among multiple billing contacts is deferred ('confirm the approved contact-selection ... rules'); only the equally-applicable ambiguous case is decided (send none).

verdicts.quote: The automation owns the durable occurrence status, scoped identifiers, attempt identity, and bounded outcome metadata.
verdicts.missing: No record of what was sent is kept ('No separate product-side copy of the message ... is required'), and the history is not shown on the invoice.

verdicts.quote: identifies the billing sender and customer-visible invoice reference, gives the due date and current outstanding amount with currency, and directs the recipient to review or pay through their usual billing route
Account operators with configuration permission can read and change it. ... The billing owner must identify the target account, authorized configuration entry point and roles
verdicts.missing: The actual roles are left open, and nothing says who may stop a single reminder by hand; manual sends are out of scope.

verdicts.quote: An authorized operator activates reminders for a named billing account. ... Once off is committed, pending work cannot receive a new dispatch authorization.
verdicts.missing: No global off switch and no preview or dry run; manual resend is explicitly out of scope.

verdicts.quote: An authorized operator can distinguish eligibility or pending work, a delivery-channel acceptance, and a delivery failure or unresolved result.
The maximum allowed age for catch-up and handling of very old invoices are open product decisions.
verdicts.missing: No actual bound on sending volume or on how late a reminder may still go out; both are left as open bounds.

verdicts.quote: Invoice issuance, payment collection and allocation, invoice balances and due dates, and access to invoices remain under their existing billing rules. Reminder automation does not change those rules.
